subject: Civic Education
competence: Appreciates the diversity of the world of work through active exploration of regional employment sectors and professions.
lesson: Explains the diversity of world of work. Activity “Let’s undentify world of work” Time 40 minutes: Provincial Career Simulation & Scenario Debate
unique_learning_outcome: Explains the diversity of world of work. Activity “Let’s undentify world of work” Time 40 minutes
the_entrance: The teacher facilitates a fast-paced 5-minute provincial hook by projecting a map of Sri Lanka on the chalkboard and challenging the six seated groups to act as regional development advisors. The teacher asks, 'If you were advising the Nuwara Eliya district or Hambantota port zone, what diverse blend of traditional farming and modern tech careers would keep your youth employed?' Students immediately huddle in their teams of five, with Leaders assigning roles and Scribes jotting down initial regional industries like tea cultivation, marine engineering, and software freelancing to launch the simulation.

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher circulates among the six group islands acting as a chief economic advisor, prompting teams with targeted questions like, 'How does your district balance primary agricultural labor with emerging digital service jobs?' The teacher observes collaboration, ensures all team members contribute, and provides scaffolding for identifying specialized vocations.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Students collaborate intensely within their groups of five to analyze their assigned Sri Lankan provincial profile. The Scribe and Leader guide the discussion while the Civic Investigator cross-checks agricultural and industrial job data against textbook definitions of the world of work, drafting a comprehensive Provincial Career Blueprint on chart paper.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_method: Provincial Career Blueprint Drafting and Economic Roleplay
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: District profile task sheets, chart paper, colored markers, student notebooks

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher acts as moderator for the rapid-fire floor debate, inviting Spokespersons to present their regional models and challenging opposing groups to critique professional diversity gaps. The teacher guides constructive peer evaluation on how vocational variety prevents regional unemployment.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: The Spokesperson for each group presents their Provincial Career Blueprint to the class, defending why their unique mix of traditional and modern careers sustains local growth. Meanwhile, Timekeepers manage presentation pacing and Inquirers respectfully challenge neighboring groups with questions about job sustainability.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_method: Inter-Provincial Scenario Debate and Sector Defense
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Completed Provincial Career Blueprint charts, chalkboard, chalk

summary: In a concise 2-minute synthesis, the teacher and students consolidate that the Sri Lankan world of work is a rich tapestry spanning agriculture, industry, and diverse modern services, proving that professional variety is vital for balanced regional development and personal readiness.
assessment_and_feedback_whole_lesson: Formative evaluation is conducted through observation of group collaboration, accuracy of the Provincial Career Blueprint, and the quality of peer argumentation during the scenario debate, evaluated against criteria including introducing the world of work, naming diverse jobs, and expressing personal readiness for employment.
post_activity: Students engage in a 5-minute Pass-the-Concept Dilemma Challenge where the teacher passes a local employment scenario card (e.g., transitioning an agrarian village to agro-technology) to Group 1. The student holding the card has 30 seconds to name one new diverse career addition and pass it to the next group, creating a rapid chain of vocational insights until all teams have defended a unique addition.

selected_activity:
Activity: Provincial Career Simulation & Scenario Debate
Approach: Students step into the shoes of regional development advisors in different Sri Lankan provinces, evaluating the challenges and diversity of professions required to sustain local communities.
Student task: Each group receives a unique Sri Lankan provincial profile (e.g., plantation sector in Nuwara Eliya, fishing and port logistics in Hambantota, tech-agro farming in Anuradhapura). They debate and list the diverse mix of traditional and modern careers vital for that region's growth.
Teacher facilitation: Acts as timekeeper and chief advisor, circulating among the 6 islands to challenge groups to justify why professional diversity is essential to prevent regional unemployment.
Expected output: A Provincial Career Blueprint chart detailing essential traditional and emerging occupations for a specific Sri Lankan district.
Grouping: 6 teams (6 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer
